segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for November 26th, 2026.
We've got 17 updates, including insights on humanoid mass production, factory robotics training, and advanced AI vision integration.
From Humanoids Daily, XPENG Details Mass-Production IRON Humanoid at AI Day 2026, Confirms Unisex Form Factor and VLA 3.0.

This report details the unveiling of the mass-production iteration of the IRON humanoid robot, confirming a standardized unisex form factor and the utilization of the Turing Physical AI Architecture version three point zero.
The robot employs XPENG's architecture across three AI chips to achieve seventy-six degrees of freedom and comprehensive tactile sensing.
Hardware mass production is slated to commence in January two thousand twenty-seven on an automated line, with a commercial launch targeted for the second quarter of two thousand twenty-seven.
The IRON model incorporates advanced safety mechanisms, including collision mitigation protocols and a solid-state battery capable of withstanding two hundred degrees Celsius.
The company intends to deliver the IRON as a configurable work partner via skill packs and subscription plans following delivery.
This development signals a tangible progression toward deployable, standardized humanoid robotics within the near future.
From Robotics & Automation News, Volvo Cars begins training Hexagon humanoid robots for factory work.
This report details the initiative where Volvo Cars is training Hexagon AEON humanoid robots at its Ghent plant with the goal of integrating them into production by mid-2027.

The facility serves as the first Volvo plant to trial these robots, where the training process employs imitation learning, starting with precise component placement and subsequently progressing to more complex tasks alongside human workers and existing automation.
This exploration focuses on the mobility and capability of humanoid robots within existing factory settings to enhance safety, flexibility, and operational efficiency in automotive manufacturing.
This development signals a tangible step in deploying advanced robotics within complex industrial environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Universal Robots brings Inbolt’s 3D AI vision directly onto its Gen 7 robots".

This report details the integration of Inbolt’s 3D AI vision system directly into the Universal Robots Gen 7 robots, enabling real-time component identification and trajectory adjustment during production.
The integration involves running the Inbolt Standard software natively on the robot's controller, which eliminates the requirement for separate computing hardware.
This integration simplifies robotic vision by reducing the need for customized jigs and fixtures when handling new products.
The system supports diverse industrial applications and facilitates rapid training on new components using CAD files.
This development signifies a step toward more flexible and adaptive robotic systems in manufacturing.
From The Robot Report, "FCC should focus on robot security, not country of origin".

This segment addresses the prioritization of regulatory focus for robot security, asserting that the security boundary resides in the software and control mechanisms rather than the physical origin of the hardware.
The report indicates that regulated systems require standards concerning secure code updates, data handling protocols, and access controls.
This focus necessitates establishing standards for the provenance of control, vulnerability patching procedures, and independent safety layers for artificial intelligence systems.
Ultimately, the report concludes that regulation must concentrate on the entity controlling the code and the methods used for managing remote access.
The technology sector must address these software-centric security requirements immediately to establish effective regulatory frameworks.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "How DARPA Challenged Teams to Bring Robots Into Disaster Triage".

This story details a grand challenge organized by DARPA aimed at demonstrating the life-saving potential of robots in emergency triage situations, with the key result being the demonstration of robotic capability in disaster scenarios.
Teams competed to develop and deploy robotic solutions for these critical tasks.

During the finals, a Spot robot from the University of Maryland’s RoboScout team was shown surveying the area, highlighting the practical application of robotics in disaster response through the execution of complex surveying duties.
This event demonstrated the feasibility of utilizing robotic systems for immediate assessment and aid in chaotic environments.
The successful completion of this challenge underscores the advancement of robotics in critical response applications for future deployment.
From Robotics & Automation News, "When robots lose contact: Research examines the resilience of decentralized robot swarms".
This story investigates the resilience of decentralized robot swarms when communication is lost, finding that disconnected robots can still perform useful work based on their local memory.
The research involved a simulation comparing decentralized methods, such as M-PSO, against leader-based approaches during pressure vessel inspection under extreme conditions.
Decentralized coordination demonstrated a higher success rate in local location estimation compared to leader-based methods.
However, the study also indicated that while decentralized systems maintain local information, communication failures impede the easy retrieval of that stored data.
This suggests that decentralized intelligence is beneficial for data preservation, but requires further engineering for reliable information transmission in complex systems.
The findings point toward the importance of developing robust communication protocols for future autonomous swarm applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Heavy metal acrobatics: Researchers teach five-ton construction vehicle to balance on two wheels".
This story details the development of an artificial intelligence capable of enabling a five-ton skid-steer loader to balance and perform complex maneuvers on two wheels.
Researchers utilized reinforcement learning to train an AI by collecting operational data to develop a neural network predicting actuator behavior for autonomous control.
The system successfully demonstrated stationary balancing, in-place spinning, and navigating terrain with undulations up to seventy-five centimeters.
The reinforcement learning approach exhibited greater capability in certain demanding maneuvers when compared to a conventional model predictive control system.
This research establishes a foundation for future autonomous control of heavy machinery across various industries.
From Humanoid.guide, KIRO plans KAREX-M humanoid for Antarctic heavy lifting.
This report details the development of a hybrid mobile humanoid system intended for installing and maintaining observation infrastructure in Antarctica.
The project has secured six billion won in funding with the objective of developing two integrated platforms for Antarctic missions around the year 2030.
The KAREX-M features a wheel or track base and a hydraulic dual-arm upper body engineered for heavy lifting and manipulation.

The system incorporates a battery generator hybrid power system capable of up to two hundred kilometers of travel and integrates artificial intelligence for efficient route planning and remote operation.
Staged testing is planned, targeting the deployment of these robots for infrastructure construction in the Antarctic by 2030.
This development signals a trajectory toward applying advanced robotics in extreme environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, Exotec helps Fnac Darty handle Black Friday rush with refurbished and rented robots.

This report details a partnership where Exotec automated the Massy logistics facility for Fnac Darty during the Black Friday period, increasing order processing capacity through the deployment of refurbished robots and a rental system.
The automation system incorporated thirty-six robots and dedicated storage locations to enhance throughput.
During peak demand, the retailer utilized the ability to rent supplementary robots, effectively doubling processing capacity.

A significant aspect of the implementation involved the reuse of equipment from a prior operation, showcasing a modular approach that allows for flexible capacity expansion without substantial initial capital expenditure.
This case illustrates the practical application of modular robotics in high-demand retail logistics.
From Robotics & Automation News, AutomationML to join OPC Foundation to strengthen industrial interoperability.
This story concerns the planned integration of AutomationML technology with the OPC Foundation to establish a unified framework for industrial interoperability.
AutomationML is scheduled to join the OPC Foundation by January 1, 2027, facilitating the transfer of AutomationML's technology to the Foundation to create a unified framework.
This integration aims to establish a consistent method for exchanging engineering and operational information across automation systems, which supports digital twins and artificial intelligence.

The unification seeks to preserve the meaning of information throughout the entire industrial lifecycle, from engineering to decommissioning, thereby reducing data silos between engineering and operational data for enhanced interoperability.
This unification signals a move toward more cohesive data standards within the industrial technology sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Angelini Technologies acquires stake in Oversonic Robotics to support international expansion.
This report details the acquisition of a stake in Oversonic Robotics by Angelini Technologies to facilitate industrial growth and international expansion.
Angelini brings fifty years of industrial automation expertise and logistics robotics knowledge to the company.
This investment is intended to increase Oversonic Robotics manufacturing capacity and extend its robotics solutions into global markets, with a specific focus on the United States.
Oversonic Robotics developed the cognitive humanoid robot RoBee, which is designed for deployment in both industrial and healthcare sectors.
The partnership establishes a combination of Oversonic's innovation with Angelini's extensive industrial experience for future growth.
This collaboration signals a strategic move toward integrating specialized expertise with advanced robotics technology in the global market.
From Humanoid.guide, Noetix Boomy launches crowdfunding with a three thousand five hundred ninety nine entry price.
This report details the launch of a crowdfunding campaign for the Boomy programmable humanoid robot, setting an entry pledge of three thousand five hundred ninety nine dollars.

The robot is designed for programming experiments, supporting graphical blocks, Python, and C++, and possesses the capability for self-balanced walking at up to one meter per second, incorporating twenty one degrees of freedom.
The standard model includes onboard machine learning and vision capabilities, while an upgraded Edu version includes enhanced computing power and a depth camera.
This development signals continued movement in the accessibility and complexity of programmable humanoid robotics.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel".
This report details the development of an experimental bionic hand capable of providing sensory feedback to the user.
The research involved connecting a prosthetic hand to the nerves in the forearm to enable the perception of pressure.

A participant in a University of Utah clinical trial, Avi Davidson, was the first to use this device independently, which required surgically implanting electrodes into nerves and training a computer system to translate nerve signals into both movement control and sensation.
Despite functional improvements, Davidson reported experiences of phantom pain and wrist strain, which directs ongoing research into the technology's long-term implications.
This advancement signals further progress in interfacing artificial systems with the human nervous system.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Designing Robot Gripper Fingers for Repeatable Changeovers"
details the methodology for ensuring consistent workpiece positioning across different robot installations.
This approach necessitates tracing requirements from the receiving operation through the tooling to define the necessary geometric relationships and acceptance criteria.
Locating features must be defined independently from fasteners, and reference surfaces require accessibility for inspection.
A spare-parts policy and rigorous post-change testing are identified as crucial elements for predictable maintenance.
Ultimately, a replacement must restore a known arrangement with documented evidence confirming adherence to process requirements.
This work establishes a framework for manufacturing highly adaptable robotic end-effectors.
The industry should focus on developing standardized interfaces for machine tooling.
From The Robot Report, "How Vention is cutting factory programming from weeks to minutes".
This story details how the company Vention is reducing the time required for factory programming from weeks to mere minutes.
Etienne Lacroix, CEO and Founder of Vention, has a background developing industrial technologies at McKinsey and GE.
Vention facilitates the process by allowing customers to select from multiple workcell templates when designing a workcell.
This advancement emphasizes the necessity of effectively implementing robotics in real-world manufacturing environments.
Furthermore, Intel is contributing to this development by providing a robotics platform incorporating artificial intelligence, sensing, and real-time control capabilities.
This technological convergence points toward accelerated deployment of intelligent automation systems across industrial sectors.
From Robohub, "Space robotics: notes from an IROS 2026 plenary session"

reports on discussions held by speakers from NASA, JAXA, and academia concerning the role of robots in lunar exploration, human spaceflight, and orbital work, with potential applications including cargo unloading, lunar infrastructure construction, and space debris removal.
Speakers detailed the need for robotic systems in lunar exploration, focusing on applications such as unloading cargo and building lunar infrastructure.
NASA is shifting focus toward MoonBase, necessitating robotic systems for habitat construction, resource utilization, and in-situ resource utilization.
Furthermore, autonomous robotics is identified as critical for future deep-space missions requiring reduced human intervention.
This research indicates a strong linkage between space robotics and terrestrial industries like construction, logistics, and mining.
The advancements in this field suggest increased investment and development across the AI and technology sectors for future space exploration.
From Robotics & Automation News, Physical AI model outpaces human operator in robot manipulation tests.
This report details performance benchmarks where an AI model demonstrated superior speed in executing everyday robotic manipulation tasks compared to a human operator.
The study involved testing several physical AI models against human performance in manipulation scenarios.
The FLUX-mimic-x model achieved a median completion time of eleven seconds for these tasks, contrasting with a median time of twenty-seven seconds recorded for the human participant.
Furthermore, another model named Praxis-1 exhibited the capability to recover from errors during the task execution process.

The research indicates that the most reliable dedicated robot models on the leaderboard are utilizing video models instead of traditional vision-language models, suggesting a significant shift toward world-action models within the robotics industry.
This development points toward increased expectations for autonomous, real-world action capabilities in future robotic systems.

From silicon to sentience, the future is assembling itself.
